title: Cap. IX Sol: willing to save anyone if he believes is not decreeing to work faith in everyone — Remonstrants confuse the two; conditional will = faith-salvation nexus
pass_a_gloss: Let the Remonstrants therefore understand, who everywhere urge this, that it is one thing seriously to will to save any man if he believe, another to decree to work in any man that he believe. God can will the former without any simulation, although as to some he has decreed not to will the latter in their reprobation. Here nevertheless in passing it will not be beside the point to warn, when we say that God wills to save any man if he believe, that we denote by this conditioned will nothing other than that eternal and inviolable ordination of God concerning the indissoluble nexus of faith and salvation: on account of which nexus this promise is verified of any elect or non-elect person, If thou shalt have believed, thou shalt be saved. Meanwhile the will of God is not understood to be conversant about the salvation of the non-elect man as if suspended or uncertain; but by such forms of speaking this is affirmed, that if the condition of faith were posited in the object, there would also be in God an actual will of saving such a person: which suffices unto excluding that simulation which they endeavor to fasten upon God.
pass_b_english: So let the Remonstrants, who press this everywhere, understand: it is one thing seriously to will to save anyone if he believes, another to decree to work in anyone so that he believes. God can will the first without any simulation, even while for some he has decreed not to will the second in their reprobation. One passing note: when we say God wills to save anyone if he believes, by that conditioned will we mean only God's eternal inviolable ordination of the indissoluble bond of faith and salvation — for which bond the promise If you believe, you will be saved holds true of any elect or non-elect person. God's will is not thereby pictured as hanging uncertain over a non-elect man's salvation; such speech only affirms that if the faith-condition were set in the object, God would also actually will to save that person — enough to shut out the simulation they try to pin on God.
source_text: Intelligant itaque Remonstrantes, qui hoc passim urgent, aliud esse velle serio quemlibet hominem servare si credat, aliud decernere operari in quolibet homine ut credat. Potest Deus velle prius absque omni simulatione, quamvis quoad quosdam decreverit nolle posterius in illorum reprobatione. Hic tamen in transcursu illud monere haud abs re erit, cum dicimus Deum velle servare quemlibet hominem si credat, nos nihil aliud denotare per hanc conditionatam voluntatem, quam aeternam illam et inviolabilem Dei ordinationem de nexu indissolubili fidei et salutis: propter quem nexum de qualibet persona electa vel non-electa verificatur haec promissio, Si credideris, salvus eris. Interim voluntas Dei non intelligitur versari circa salutem hominis non-electi quasi suspensa aut incerta; sed hujusmodi loquendi formulis id affirmatur, si conditio fidei in objecto poneretur, esset etiam in Deo voluntas actualis talem personam servandi: quod sufficit ad excludendam illam simulationem quam Deo impingere conantur.
